scope: 131 print-only identities; prospective tabletop probes, not measured observations
goal: For each focus card, demonstrate a real choice, payoff net of Command and Actions, and legal counterplay. A failed probe is a reason to consider replacement, not automated proof of uselessness.

focus.opportunity: An Archer is in Rear; the opposing Frontline Guard is not a legal basic Archer Attack target and needs to be Shaken to open a Raider Incursion.
focus.comparison: Compare paying 2C plus an Action to Shake any opposing rank with a free basic Archer Attack that can target Rear only and be screened.
focus.failure_signal: If any-rank Shaken is always better than other 2C Tactics without a distinct setup, restrict or reprice it.

focus.opportunity: An opposing King/Captain Force is active with another opposing formation in the same Front; one is named.
focus.comparison: Compare its Shaken and −1 splash to They Let Them Through's single-formation ACTION/Name shutdown at the same 1C.
focus.failure_signal: If the new effect still never wins a different trade from They Let Them Through, redesign it.

focus.opportunity: A Scout or Ship observes a newly set enemy Stratagem in the same or an adjacent Front.
focus.comparison: Compare a +2 Strength reaction with playing an immediate 1C support card this Battle.
focus.failure_signal: If no Stratagem appears or the +2 cannot affect a contested Front, the Narrative is unplayable value.

focus.opportunity: A friendly Force completes a Named Formation with Brannoc while the enemy's Shaken Bonded formation carries a valuable Name or Bond.
focus.comparison: Compare Brannoc's 2C +1 Strength and one-time attached-card removal with a 1C Name and an independent 1C Tactic or a 1C Seized the Standard Bond.
focus.failure_signal: If the Shaken enemy never offers an attachment at completion or it produces unanswerable permanent snowball, narrow or soften the benefit.

focus.opportunity: A Scout or Captain holds a Front with an opposing face-down Stratagem and a legal friendly Move that could alter a flank.
focus.comparison: Compare spending 1C/Action to reveal a specific hidden plan and Move with the same Bond played without any plan or a regular Maneuver.
focus.failure_signal: If scouting information cannot change the movement decision, the two benefits are merely decorative and the zero-Strength Bond may be weak.

focus.opportunity: An attached Name's continuous or ACTION effect would be suppressed by a legal opposing Tactic.
focus.comparison: Compare protection of Name text with a +Strength Bond and simply replaying the effect next Battle.
focus.failure_signal: If the opponent lacks suppression, the Bond's 1 Strength is its entire floor.

focus.opportunity: An Exhausted friendly Force directly ahead could reach a flanked enemy only by Maneuvering while Exhausted, with this Bond already attached behind.
focus.comparison: Compare its 1C continuing Maneuver permission with a single Move Order or cleansing the Exhaustion first.
focus.failure_signal: If the directly-ahead geometry almost never occurs, replace this conditional permission with a more immediate decision.

focus.opportunity: Another friendly Named Human formation is already in play when Eira completes her own Named Formation and would draw two cards.
focus.comparison: Compare Eira's conditional draw-two at 2C with a cheap Name and a separate 0C Scout-supported Order.
focus.failure_signal: If the prerequisite cannot be achieved early enough to affect Action choices, its card-flow reward is delayed too long.

focus.opportunity: An Elian Named Formation can spend 1 Command and one Action to Move into a newly legal Raider, Archer, Skirmisher or Rider basic Attack target.
focus.comparison: Compare its paid Move-plus-unused-Attack with a normal 1C Maneuver followed by a second Attack Action; track once-per-Battle Attack use.
focus.failure_signal: If an ordinary Attack was already possible or the next Action is always spent on Force deployment, the card-granted combination may be too powerful or unnecessary.

focus.opportunity: A King or Captain leads multiple Human formations across two active adjacent Fronts at the post-Opening-Orders resolution reveal.
focus.comparison: Compare 2C cross-Front Strength from Every Banner with a 1C single-Front opening Commit, The Center Must Hold, and using the Action to deploy another Force earlier.
focus.failure_signal: If the final simultaneous Strength swing decides several full-margin Front losses with no viable earlier response, revise reach or price.

focus.opportunity: One Bonded Archer can declare an Opening Strike against an opposing Middle Force while an ordinary Archer Strike against Rear would be screened or less relevant.
focus.comparison: Compare paying 1C and a Narrative PLAY Action for one Middle-target Opening Strike with relying on The Crow Archers when the opposing Frontline is empty.
focus.failure_signal: If middle-target Strikes are seldom legal or the existing Crow Archers provide the same answer reliably, the Narrative adds little tactical value.

focus.opportunity: A Bonded formation has a legal opening Maneuver and a second adjacent empty legal position that creates a flank or changes which Front it defends.
focus.comparison: Compare one free two-position Opening Maneuver against the regular one-position Opening Maneuver and the hidden Rider-specific Battle Turned East extension.
focus.failure_signal: If another Move only repositions without changing an Attack, flank or final Front result, this 1C zero-Strength Bond may be too narrow.

focus.opportunity: A formation becomes Named with Iria while an opposing Stratagem is set and a local legal Move could change which Front is threatened.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C Name's peek plus friendly Move with a regular Maneuver on that Named Formation and a 1C scouting-only Name.
focus.failure_signal: If peeking never changes the intended Move, record the positional effect separately from the information payoff.

focus.opportunity: Kael played as Name completes a formation while a hidden Stratagem exists in its Front and a legal positional response is available.
focus.comparison: Compare Kael's cheap Name-mode peek and Move with its more expensive Force-mode two-step ACTION and a normal 1C Name.
focus.failure_signal: If no hidden plan or legal Move can affect an Attack or Front result, the Hero Name may still be selected only because it costs less.

focus.opportunity: A friendly Rider or Scout occupies a Front whose adjacent active position is legally empty; playing the Bond could create a Rider flank or uncover a target.
focus.comparison: Compare a 1C Bond PLAY that Moves a Rider/Scout with a 1C Maneuver requiring Named status and a static +1 Strength Bond.
focus.failure_signal: If the Move is usually identical to choosing the initial position or never changes Attack eligibility, the extra tempo is overstated.

focus.opportunity: An Exhausted friendly Force directly behind a Bonded formation needs a legal Maneuver to prevent an adjacent flank or retreat.
focus.comparison: Compare its ongoing rearward Maneuver permission with the forward permission on Covered the Withdrawal of and a recovery Order.
focus.failure_signal: If the exact geometry rarely produces an Action-worthy Maneuver, this support role is too narrow.

focus.opportunity: A new Named Formation with Lysa may inspect an opponent's hand and place Guarded on a vulnerable friendly Force in its Front.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C Name's hand information and Guarded with Mara's hand-peek plus Move and with a 1C Guarded Bond.
focus.failure_signal: If hand information never affects where to protect or Guarded is usually redundant, Lysa has no distinctive practical purpose.

focus.opportunity: A Bond completes a Formation in a contested Front and its +1 this Battle would flip the Front.
focus.comparison: Compare 1C Bond's permanent Strength plus temporary bonus against other 1C Bonds.
focus.failure_signal: If the one-turn bonus does not alter result, it still enables Named; record that separately.

focus.opportunity: A 4C Namar completes a Named Formation and can discount an additional Bond or Name play in the same Front next turn.
focus.comparison: Compare Namar's Command and Action setup cost against two cheaper Names and a direct Bond play at normal Command.
focus.failure_signal: If the 4C Name never repays its premium during a real Battle, reconsider its orchestration payoff.

focus.opportunity: A prepared Bond and prepared Name occupy nearby positions while Nara could attach one of them immediately or as a once-per-Battle ACTION.
focus.comparison: Compare the Hero's Force- and Name-mode preparation effects with the ordinary two-step deployment and Field Train.
focus.failure_signal: If players never prepare enough layers to activate Nara or its mode choices feel identical, its unusual preparation role needs work.

focus.opportunity: Neris Force mode has an unused basic Rider Attack and can Move into a position with a legal flanked enemy target.
focus.comparison: Compare the 4C Hero's once-per-Battle Move-plus-Attack ACTION with the 3C Vardai's 1C paid Move-plus-Attack and Neris's 2C Name mode.
focus.failure_signal: If the Force mode remains inferior to Vardai or the Hero's Name mode in most states, its Force premium may be wasted.

focus.opportunity: Two adjacent active Fronts each have movable Formations with all rank placements legal.
focus.comparison: Compare one Action/3C front-column exchange and +2 to individual Moves across several turns.
focus.failure_signal: If a legal beneficial exchange cannot be staged, the card is effectively dormant.

focus.opportunity: After losing an early Front, the player has less Command and a friendly formation can Move to protect a rank or create an Incursion target.
focus.comparison: Compare this 1C Bond's recovery-plus-Move with a separate 1C Maneuver or spending that Action on permanent Force Strength.
focus.failure_signal: If players recover Command but almost never use the Move, it is still mostly economy text rather than comeback tactics.

focus.opportunity: A Captain is present while a friendly persistent Force blocks a crucial Frontline position and discarding it would regain two Command.
focus.comparison: Compare sacrificing the Force and its attachments for only two Command with the Order's alternative swap and a normal Maneuver.
focus.failure_signal: If the discard branch is never chosen outside inevitable Collapse, it should remain an emergency option rather than a primary battle action.

focus.opportunity: Rovan is played as a Force in Frontline against a weaker opposing defender with a legal space behind it.
focus.comparison: Compare the 5C Hero's Shaken-plus-optional-push with Iron Boars' Shaken on PLAY and a separate forced-retreat Tactic.
focus.failure_signal: If Gatebreaker cannot displace troops often enough to justify its Hero allowance or reliably locks defenders out, rebalance its payoff.

focus.opportunity: An opposing Bonded Formation has spent an Action and Command on an attachment important to its Named status, and this Bond can return that component.
focus.comparison: Compare a 1C attached Bond that returns a permanent opposing Bond with a 2C hostile Tactic and a basic Attack.
focus.failure_signal: If the one-Action exchange removes too much persistent investment without meaningful counterplay, tighten this card rather than adding casualties.

focus.opportunity: A Shaken/Exhausted named Rider needs row movement and can still Maneuver due to Sela.
focus.comparison: Compare two movement permissions with free deployment and normal Maneuver restrictions.
focus.failure_signal: If rank change is never worthwhile, investigate narrow movement rather than price.

focus.opportunity: A Scout in Rear can legally Move toward a threatened Front while the player benefits from drawing one new card.
focus.comparison: Compare the free-Command Order's one Action for Scout movement and one draw with the normal 1C Named Maneuver or cycling two cards.
focus.failure_signal: If Scout movement is usually illegal or the Order is used solely as free card filtering, its tactical purpose is too weak.

focus.opportunity: Serai played as Name commands an Archer that can reposition across active Fronts to alter a Guard screen or threaten a Rear Force.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C paid repeatable Archer Move with simply deploying another Archer or paying for an ordinary Named Maneuver.
focus.failure_signal: If repeated moves never unlock different targets or are almost always better than other Name ACTIONs, revisit this Queen's mode value.

focus.opportunity: A Raider or Skirmisher formation in an active Front needs a Move to open an Incursion after an opponent in that Front was Shaken.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C zero-Strength Bond and one free Move with the 1C Marched With Strength Bond and a separate 1C Maneuver.
focus.failure_signal: If the Shaken condition almost never overlaps a legal useful Move, replace the zero-Strength Bond's payoff.

focus.opportunity: A prepared Name is in the same Front as an unNamed Force and this Bond can complete it.
focus.comparison: Compare 0-Strength Bond + immediate attachment with a normal +1 Bond and an ordinary Name play.
focus.failure_signal: If it requires more setup than saved Actions, it is redundant.

focus.opportunity: A prepared Name/Bond can attach to the Force directly ahead as this Bond is played.
focus.comparison: Compare extra prep Action and 0-Strength Bond with ordinary direct attachment.
focus.failure_signal: If the preparation shortcut does not save time or grant a Named completion, flag.

focus.opportunity: A Bonded Middle formation can tax enemy Tactics targeting a valuable friendly Rear unit.
focus.comparison: Compare 0-Strength defensive Bond with a +1-Strength Bond and a Guard screen.
focus.failure_signal: If tax has no practical deterrent, identify better trigger.

focus.opportunity: A 3-Strength Aradai is played into Frontline opposite a 3-Strength defender with an opposing Rear target; its temporary -1 permits an immediate later Raider Incursion.
focus.comparison: Compare Aradai's 3C baseline body and one-Battle defender -1 with Thirty Spears at 2C (no Attack) and a stronger 4C Raider.
focus.failure_signal: If the local -1 seldom opens a legal Raider Attack before Shaken clears, its odd-Strength compensation is too situational.

focus.opportunity: A player planned an Archer Opening Strike in slot 2, while an opponent Strikes an allied Force in slot 1 and The Archers Were Ready could counterattack.
focus.comparison: Compare using the Archer's Attack in response to the first Strike versus preserving it for the planned second Strike, checking Guard screening and legal targets after Maneuvers.
focus.failure_signal: If players can make both the reactive Archer Attack and the later Strike with the same Force, the once-per-Battle Attack allowance was implemented incorrectly.

focus.opportunity: A Named Middle Banner Singers faces an opponent holding a Tactic that targets another friendly formation here.
focus.comparison: Compare 3C/three-layer setup with the same turn spent adding a higher Strength Force.
focus.failure_signal: If +1 hostile cost never prevents or changes a Tactic choice, the effect is decoration.

focus.opportunity: Several Hero or Named Formations are active in neighboring Fronts and a 2C Narrative would add widespread temporary Strength.
focus.comparison: Compare the immediate passive Strength total with one 2C tactical Narrative that moves or protects troops during the Battle.
focus.failure_signal: If mass Strength repeatedly dominates tactical positional choices, reduce its scope before adding new combat rules.

focus.opportunity: A Rider moves after plan is set; the extra step permits a new flank or avoids a counterattack.
focus.comparison: Compare plan set +1C with two ordinary Maneuvers and with no plan.
focus.failure_signal: If the extra step is illegal or redundant, record failure.

focus.opportunity: An opposing Shaken Named formation holds a valuable Bond or Name and The Black Pursuers can spend one Action and 1 Command to return it.
focus.comparison: Compare its 1 Command ACTION after an Archer/Skirmisher Shake with another Attack, or using a hostile Tactic instead.
focus.failure_signal: If a legal attached target rarely remains Shaken or the bounce has no tactical payoff, the extra Action is unattractive.

focus.opportunity: A King or Captain supports a Front with another friendly formation that could shift ranks or neighboring active Fronts during resolution.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C hidden plan's commanded Move and +2 with the broader 2C Every Banner Turned Toward Them mass Strength reward.
focus.failure_signal: If moving at the simultaneous window produces unclear eligibility or dominates both neighboring Fronts, narrow the effect.

focus.opportunity: An opposing Force can first be Exhausted on Narrative PLAY and later be Shaken through a separately spent Action with an Archer present.
focus.comparison: Compare two Actions and 2C for the combined marker pressure with a single 2C Tactic that already Shakes one opposing Force.
focus.failure_signal: If the second Action almost never changes the Front winner, simplify the delayed sequence instead of adding more triggers.

focus.opportunity: In Battle II, another friendly Raider can be advanced by The Damar to Frontline, gaining its first legal target for a basic Raider Attack in one paid Action.
focus.comparison: Compare 4C Damar plus one free newly legal Attack with deploying a 3C line Force and then separately spending Actions to Move and Attack.
focus.failure_signal: If the extra Command premium is paid but the free Attack is almost never legally created, coordinated advance is overpriced.

focus.opportunity: A Bonded but Unnamed Rider/Skirmisher has an adjacent Front with a legal better position.
focus.comparison: Compare one-Command Maneuver to completing a Name before moving.
focus.failure_signal: If the Bond-only permission does not save an Action or Command, flag.

focus.opportunity: During Battle II, a Bonded Force in an active Front is missing a Name and you hold The Field Train plus that Name; playing Field Train in Middle is legal.
focus.comparison: Compare Field Train's 3C/2-Strength body and a no-extra-Action Name play (full Name Command paid, Guarded on completion) against spending one Action on each card or playing a stronger Force.
focus.failure_signal: If spending 3C for the weak Field Train body and saved Action never changes the Front or next-turn options, its hand deployment still fails the tempo test.

focus.opportunity: During Battle I, one Human already holds Middle and The Fifty Men are played into Frontline, activating their temporary one-Battle +1 Strength reward.
focus.comparison: Compare the 4C/5-Strength conditional temporary bonus against a 4C/4-Strength Guard with screening or the 2C Thirty Spears simple body.
focus.failure_signal: If conditional +1 makes The Fifty Men dominate other 4C roles every Battle, compensation overshoots the odd-Strength rounding margin.

focus.opportunity: An outer Front is active with a Guard, Archer or Stronghold that could Move before scoring and change local or adjacent Front results.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C secret reposition-and-+2 with a simple +2 defence that leaves the formation fixed and the Rider flank unchanged.
focus.failure_signal: If the outer-Front timing gate produces no legal meaningful Move, note the dead setup rather than calling the card useful.

focus.opportunity: An Unnamed or Exhausted Grey Rider Maneuvers across an active Front boundary, causing an opposing Frontline to become flanked and eligible for its basic Rider Attack.
focus.comparison: Compare Grey Riders' single paid Maneuver plus unused Rider Attack with an ordinary Named Rider's two separate Actions and permanent Strength deployment.
focus.failure_signal: If new legal Rider targets rarely appear, the expensive combined tempo does not earn its 4C printed price.

focus.opportunity: At resolution, only your side has Named Formation and your Front is tied or losing by exactly 1.
focus.comparison: Compare its 1C resolution swing to saving the hidden-plan action for a Force/Name earlier.
focus.failure_signal: If only late rare board states work, treat as a specialist rather than automatic keeper.

focus.opportunity: Two prepared components can be attached to Forces in the same Front, one of which becomes Named.
focus.comparison: Compare the cost and Actions of preparing, playing House of Reed and using its attachment ACTION with straightforward attachment to that same Force.
focus.failure_signal: If extra Actions and 4C cannot produce earlier or stronger Named completion, flag.

focus.opportunity: You have an exposed high-value Frontline Force and an empty Middle. Play Ilyri in Middle, then swap the friendly Forces and Guard the displaced Force.
focus.comparison: Compare to putting Ilyri in Frontline normally and to spending 3C on a 3-Strength Force.
focus.failure_signal: If swap never changes a result or protection, the 2-Strength premium has no payoff.

focus.opportunity: An opponent sets a face-down plan in the same Front while Scouts are in Middle or Rear.
focus.comparison: Compare peek plus filter with a planned Attack or unconditional card selection, counting when a useful decision follows.
focus.failure_signal: If no new decision is enabled after reading the plan, the reaction is ineffective.

focus.opportunity: A Bonded Late Banner can attach a 2–4C Name, and there is still a contested Front to decide.
focus.comparison: Compare total Command/Actions saved against a 3-Strength baseline Captain.
focus.failure_signal: If discount affects no Name before Battle closes, record setup failure.

focus.opportunity: An opponent visibly needs to play into one crowded Front while a 1C Tactic places a two-Command Tax marker there.
focus.comparison: Compare the opponent's response to this avoidable Tax with simply using a 1C Shaken Tactic on an existing Force.
focus.failure_signal: If the opponent consistently plays elsewhere or Passes without losing tempo, the threat is too weak to count as intrigue.

focus.opportunity: Your Skirmisher can move an opposing Frontline/Middle Force into a legal Rear slot.
focus.comparison: Compare 0C Tactic Action with They Had Gone Too Far's 1C fallback Shaken.
focus.failure_signal: If Rear is always full, the 0C card may be dead despite free Command.

focus.opportunity: At the single resolution reveal window, one friendly formation can legally Move to alter a flank and gain temporary +2 Strength.
focus.comparison: Compare a 1C hidden plan's Move-plus-strength with holding +2 Strength in place or having played a fresh Force earlier.
focus.failure_signal: If legal moves rarely exist at resolution, this hidden plan remains dead even though its old empty-Frontline gate is gone.

focus.opportunity: At least two Riders have legal winning Maneuvers before resolution.
focus.comparison: Compare 2C Narrative plus moves/Actions with ordinary 1C Maneuvers and permanent strengthening.
focus.failure_signal: If players never Maneuver after playing it, static +Strength alone may not justify.

focus.opportunity: A threatened Rear Force needs Archer screening but friendly Middle Guard is Shaken.
focus.comparison: Compare the unconditional Middle screening exception with an ordinary Middle Guard.
focus.failure_signal: If Shaken screening rarely matters, note it as niche defensive rather than useless.

focus.opportunity: Two friendly Raiders or Skirmishers are positioned so their legal Moves could expose a Frontline or generate a threatened Incursion.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C Narrative's two immediate Moves with two separate Maneuver Actions costing Command and with the old recurring Tactic-discount engine.
focus.failure_signal: If both Moves are rarely relevant, its ability may not beat cheaper single-Force movement or a direct hostile Tactic.

focus.opportunity: An opposing Tactic can target your Frontline Red Shields while both players have Command choices.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C Tactic tax against a normal 4C Guard body's Strength and screening.
focus.failure_signal: If opponent simply chooses other targets without cost, this may still be useful; record diversion.

focus.opportunity: In Battle II, a friendly Force in the same active Front has Exhausted and Shaken; play Middle Relief Column to remove all its negative markers and give it Guarded.
focus.comparison: Compare the 3C/3-Strength body plus immediate healing and Guarded with a separate 1C Guarded Bond, White Hands' later healing ACTION, and a normal 3C Force.
focus.failure_signal: If a legal, threatened Force rarely needs recovery and Guarded before the Battle closes, its 3-Strength baseline may be doing all the work.

focus.opportunity: A River Raider occupies Frontline, outmatches an opposing Frontline after a Shake, and can use its 1C ACTION against an attached Middle or Rear Force.
focus.comparison: Compare 4C River Raider plus 1C/action for attachment pressure with Seven Black Ships immediate PLAY attachment return using the same basic Raider legal-target check.
focus.failure_signal: If extra repeat opportunities never occur before this Raider uses its Attack, Seven Black Ships dominates its sabotage role.

focus.opportunity: An opposing hidden plan in or adjacent to your Scout's Front is strategically relevant.
focus.comparison: Compare paying 1C + a Tactic Action to force a reveal/re-set choice against playing direct Strength.
focus.failure_signal: If opponent always pays 1C and no decision changes, estimate whether tax pays.

focus.opportunity: A friendly Scout or Seer occupies the Stratagem's Front when both commanders reveal Opening Orders and one own Maneuver starts there with two possible destinations.
focus.comparison: Compare this 1C pre-set hidden redirection after seeing enemy orders with an unmodified opening Maneuver, No Step Back and The Battle Turned East.
focus.failure_signal: If redirection never changes an enemy Strike's legality, a flank or a decisive Front, it is a costly and redundant layer of intrigue.

focus.opportunity: Your Frontline Serekh directly protects a Middle formation from hostile Tactics.
focus.comparison: Compare 3C/3 Strength shield with just adding a stronger Frontline Guard.
focus.failure_signal: If the tax never influences targeting, assess whether its Guard class is enough.

focus.opportunity: During Battle II, an existing friendly Frontline Force can be moved one adjacent legal position by a new Middle Signal Company, changing a flank and allowing a card draw.
focus.comparison: Compare 3C/2-Strength Signal Company's immediate free-Action Move and optional draw against a 3C/3-Strength Damar's same-Front forward Move and a 1C ordinary Maneuver.
focus.failure_signal: If the extra movement reach and possible flank draw never compensate for one less Strength versus Damar, this remains a poor deployment choice.

focus.opportunity: A Raider or Skirmisher Opening Strike Shakes or Depletes an enemy carrying a costly Bond/Name, with The Trap Closed set face-down at that Front.
focus.comparison: Compare 2C paid hidden attachment-bounce after the negative marker with directly using Seized the Standard Of or saving Command while inflicting just the affliction.
focus.failure_signal: If the revealed trap routinely removes more permanent Strength than the opponent can recover before the uncapped margin penalty, limit its swing rather than adding more counters.

focus.opportunity: A Vardai can legally Move an adjacent empty position and then make a newly positioned basic Rider Attack; its once-per-Battle ACTION is unused.
focus.comparison: Compare its 1C once-per-Battle Move plus unused Rider Attack within one Action against a Named Rider Maneuver followed by a second Attack Action.
focus.failure_signal: If the resulting target is almost never legal, its once-per-Battle move remains an expensive Action-only reposition.

focus.opportunity: An opponent has a relevant hidden plan before your scouting ACTION; you can change the next card played based on the reveal.
focus.comparison: Compare extra ACTION spent inspecting/filtering with playing your best available card immediately.
focus.failure_signal: If the peek never changes a next action, the information is too passive.

focus.opportunity: A Force directly ahead is Shaken before Front resolution and the Middle/Rear Healer can clear it.
focus.comparison: Compare spending an ACTION to remove the condition versus playing a +Strength card and retaining tempo.
focus.failure_signal: If its healing ACTION is repeatedly weaker, the 3-Strength body alone may not justify it.

focus.opportunity: A friendly Scout or Skirmisher is present while an opposing Middle/Frontline Force can or cannot legally move one row toward Rear.
focus.comparison: Compare 1C They Had Gone Too Far (Scout or Skirmisher, Shaken fallback) with zero-Command The Line Was Baited (Skirmisher-only, Depleted on successful retreat).
focus.failure_signal: If successful movement dominates the situation and the Shaken fallback/Scout eligibility rarely matters, the two Tactics may be redundant.

focus.opportunity: A formation can legally Move across a rank or Front; a Seer is also present to grant that moved formation Guarded.
focus.comparison: Compare a 1C Narrative's immediate Move and conditional Guarded with a regular named Maneuver or playing Guarded directly.
focus.failure_signal: If no legal Move exists the card should not silently create blanket Strength; test whether the Seer actually changes which choice is best.

focus.opportunity: An opposing Named ACTION formation could activate in a contested Front.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C suppression + Name Strength loss against All Banners Forward's Shaken/second target.
focus.failure_signal: If target has no usable ACTION and no Name, record whether another Tactic was clearly better.

focus.opportunity: An opposing Named Formation has a useful Name ability and a threatening local Strength advantage; the Tactic can Shake and suppress it.
focus.comparison: Compare 2C plus an Action for combined Shaken/Name suppression with a 2C Volley or a cheaper tactic suppressing one layer.
focus.failure_signal: If permanent Named investment is too easily erased by the Tactic with no response, this effect exceeds the intended tactical pressure.

focus.opportunity: During Battle I, a friendly formation already occupies Frontline; play Thirty Spears into Middle to grant that formation +1 temporary Strength.
focus.comparison: Compare Thirty Spears at full 3C and its small +1 supporting PLAY with 3C Aradai's Frontline entry penalty and 4C Fifty Men body.
focus.failure_signal: If the support point never changes a Front or makes the 3C vanilla-style body worse than other 3C choices, revisit its role.

focus.opportunity: Tovan is attached as a Name early enough to discount multiple later Bonds and Names.
focus.comparison: Count actual Command saved and extra Actions vs 4C Name cost, and compare playing as 3C Force.
focus.failure_signal: If discount cannot repay its cost before Command recovery declines, price again.

focus.opportunity: An opposing face-down Stratagem is active in the Bond's Front or an adjacent Front and one card in hand can be exchanged.
focus.comparison: Compare the 1C zero-Strength Bond's secret peek and card filter with ordinary hand cycling and an independently deployed Scout.
focus.failure_signal: If there is no decision informed by the revealed plan or the filtered card, its printed effect remains low-impact.

focus.opportunity: A discarded Narrative provides a meaningful movement or combat choice when Yara completes a Named Formation as a Name.
focus.comparison: Compare regaining that Narrative and spending another Action with the immediate tactical advantages of other similarly priced Hero Name modes.
focus.failure_signal: If Narratives are rarely in discard before Yara is Named, treat this as an unproductive setup dependency.
